Official programme identity, teaching language, study interests, course context, faculty-wide elective choices and year-three progression. The entry-cohort OER controls credits and compulsory components.
Corroborates the cross-faculty IMPACT course titles, codes and credits. Target eligibility and choice rules come from the Communication and Information Studies regulations and prospectus.

curriculum: University of Groningen BA Communication and Information Studies, ISAT 56826, regular English-taught pathway for September 2026 entrants. The Dutch track uses specified Dutch-language modules and a Dutch thesis. The formal redesign gives Year 1 50 EC required and 10 EC chosen from two alternatives. The first listed Humane AI choice is shown using its public course title. Year 2 gives 50 EC required and one 10 EC faculty-wide course. The programme’s curriculum paragraph describes the four themes and confirms a restricted choice. The first-year AI theme continues in Humane AI in Digital Societies: Projects, also listed as 10 EC under LFW001B10 in the faculty course catalog. Year 3 gives a 30 EC minor, two 5 EC advanced communication courses, a 10 EC integrated case study and a 10 EC thesis and research seminar. The prospectus contains older tabular entries alongside newer narrative, so OER Tables 3a, 4a and 5a govern credit-bearing requirements and required courses. Groningen describes the first-semester minor and the second-semester advanced courses, organizational case and thesis. Minor choice, such as study abroad or a placement when approved, remains genuine open curriculum. The required thesis is ordinarily written in English. No separate zero-credit obligation is identified in the programme-specific curriculum.
progression: Table 7a requires Materiality of Communication before Social Media, and Year 1 completion (60 EC), Observing Communication in the Wild and Analysing Communication before the thesis seminar. The Year 1 and Year 2 work precedes those dependent components in this route. The faculty-wide introductory AI course precedes the selected projects course. The older OCASYS thesis course is listed in the transition/current calendar with a shorter prerequisite description, while the explicit September 2026 entrant rules control this cohort.
